Starfield 1.16.244.0 · 6,775 game settings · 4,818 INI settings · +3,769 Creation Kit only · built 2026-11-09 02:41 UTC

Starfield Game Settings

Every setting Starfield knows about, with its built-in default value: the game settings you change with setgs, the INI settings you change with setini or an INI file, and the extra ones only the Creation Kit uses. Starfield.esm holds records for only 2,312 game settings; the other 4,463 are built into the game and use their defaults.

By Richard Bejtlich, Richard Presents Starfield Essentials on YouTube

More Starfield tools and references: Richard Presents Development Hub.

Thank you to FearTheReap3r for pointing me to his spreadsheet, the Starfield Game Settings Database on Nexus Mods. It showed that the game has far more settings than the records in Starfield.esm, and it led to this page. More

Kinds of settings, tips and fossils

click to hide

Game settings 6,775

Tuning numbers and texts for gameplay: jump height, prices, AI timings, ship handling, menu wording. In plugins they are GMST records.

  • 6,575 are built into the game with a default value.
  • 2,112 of those also have a record in Starfield.esm, and 1,215 of those records change the default.
  • 200 exist only as a record in Starfield.esm, mostly menu texts.
  • A mod changes one by including its own GMST record. Read or change them in the console with getgs and setgs.

INI settings 4,818

Engine and display options read from the INI files (StarfieldCustom.ini, StarfieldPrefs.ini): graphics, camera, audio, controls, debugging.

  • Each has a section, written after a colon: fFPWorldFOV:Camera is fFPWorldFOV in the [Camera] section.
  • They are not plugin records, so mods can't change them through a plugin.
  • Read or change them in the console with getini and setini.

Creation Kit only 3,769

Settings that only CreationKit.exe defines: editor windows, tooltips, preview and export options, plus 30 old game settings the game itself no longer has.

  • They do nothing in the game. They are listed so a name you meet in the Creation Kit can be found here.
  • The Creation Kit's defaults are harder to read, so many are blank.

Reading the names

The first letter says the kind of value:

  • f a number with decimals, i a whole number, u a whole number that can't go below zero
  • b on or off (1 or 0), s a text, a a colour (red, green, blue, alpha)

Game settings can also have a category, the folder the Creation Kit shows them in (such as Mods or ThirdPersonCam). No category means the main group.

Settings worth trying

  • fFPWorldFOV:Camera, the first-person field of view (default 85), and fTPWorldFOV:Camera, third person (90). Wider: setini "fFPWorldFOV:Camera" 100
  • fCalendarTimeScaleSpace, how fast time passes in space. Built in as 10, but Starfield.esm sets 5: a good example of the two value columns. getgs fCalendarTimeScaleSpace
  • fJumpHeightMin, jump height (1.285875). Moon jump: setgs fJumpHeightMin 3

Console changes last until you quit, so try them on a test save first.

Mods and game settings

  • A mod changes a game setting with its own GMST record of the same name. That replaces the Starfield.esm value, or the built-in default if the game has no record for it.
  • When two mods change the same setting, the one later in the load order wins and the other's change is lost. Search for the setting's name in a conflict checker or xEdit.
  • getgs <setting> in the console shows the value that's actually in effect, whichever mod set it.
  • INI settings aren't records, so plugins can't change them; they come from your INI files and the in-game options.

Fossils and surprises bonus

Starfield runs on the same engine as Skyrim and Fallout 4, and some of their settings are still in it.

  • sAutoLockPickBrokePick: the text built into the game still says "You broke a bobby pin.", Fallout's lockpick. Starfield.esm changes it to "You used up a digipick."
  • iArrowInventoryChance: a Skyrim archery setting, the chance an arrow that hits someone ends up in their inventory. Still there (built-in 50, Starfield.esm 33), with no arrows to use it on.
  • iClassWitchhunter: a Skyrim character class, still listed in the Creation Kit.
  • bPlayerDivingEnabled: built into the game and off by default, a sign of a feature that didn't ship. We haven't tested what turning it on does.

Settings

The built-in default is the value written into the game itself. Where Starfield.esm has a record for a game setting, its value and FormID are shown too; that value is the one you get in the game unless a mod changes it. Click a console command to copy it.

No settings match. Try a shorter word, or clear the filters.

Using them in the console

  • Game settings: getgs fJumpHeightMin shows the value; setgs fJumpHeightMin 300 changes it. Give the name without its category.
  • INI settings: getini "fFPWorldFOV:Camera" shows the value; setini "fFPWorldFOV:Camera" 90 changes it. Give the name with its section, in quotes.
  • A console change lasts until you quit the game. To keep an INI setting, put it in StarfieldCustom.ini in Documents\My Games\Starfield under its section, for example [Camera] then fFPWorldFOV=90. To keep a game setting, use a mod.
  • A setting being listed doesn't mean changing it is safe or does anything visible. Many are for debugging or are no longer used. Try changes on a test save first.
  • More about these commands on the Starfield Console Commands page.

How this list was made

  • Everything was read from the Steam copy of Starfield 1.16.244.0: Starfield.exe, CreationKit.exe and Starfield.esm, plus the English string file for the texts. Nothing was copied from other lists.
  • The game creates each setting either from a ready-made entry in its data, or with a short piece of startup code that passes the name and the default value. Our tool finds both kinds, and tells game settings from INI settings by which part of the game registers them. Only names, kinds and values are published here, no game code.
  • The default values were checked against FearTheReap3r's spreadsheet: of 5,631 settings in both, 5,630 agree. The one that differs, bLeakPlanetWorldspace, is 0 in the game and 1 in the spreadsheet, probably the Creation Kit's value.
  • An INI file, the in-game options menu or a mod can change a setting. The value here is the one built into the game, or the Starfield.esm value where there is one.
  • Every game and INI setting has its default. Some defaults are set further up in the game's startup code or copied from another setting; the tool follows those too. 1,811 Creation Kit tooltip and field-label texts show "text from CreationKitTooltips.ini": the Creation Kit fills them in from that file when it starts.
  • Game updates add and remove settings; the list is regenerated after updates.
